sections.heading: Java Tutorial
paragraphs: Our Core Java programming tutorial is designed for students and working professionals. Java is an object-oriented, class-based, concurrent, secured and general-purpose computer programming language. It is a widely used robust technology.

sections.heading: What is Java?
paragraphs: Java is a programming language and a platform. Java is a high-level, robust, object-oriented and secure programming language.

Java was developed by Sun Microsystems (which is now a subsidiary of Oracle) in the year 1995. James Gosling is known as the father of Java. Before Java, its name was Oak. Since Oak was already a registered company, so James Gosling and his team changed the name from Oak to Java.
Platform: Any hardware or software environment in which a program runs is known as a platform. Since Java has a runtime environment (JRE) and API, it is called a platform.

sections.heading: Getting Started
paragraphs: Before you start coding in Java, you need to set up your system. First, install the Java Development Kit (JDK), which includes the tools required to write and run Java programs. You can download it from the official Oracle website and install it by following simple steps.

After installing the JDK, you can write your code using a text editor or an IDE like IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, or NetBeans. IDEs make coding easier by providing helpful features like auto-complete, error checking, and debugging.

sections.heading: Java Applications
paragraphs: Java is a powerful and versatile language that supports many types of applications across industries.

• Desktop Applications: Java is used to create desktop software like text editors, media players, and antivirus programs. These applications run on personal computers and provide a user-friendly interface.
• Web Applications: Java is widely used to build dynamic and secure websites. It helps developers create applications that run on web servers and can handle multiple users at the same time.
• Enterprise Applications: Java is used in large-scale business applications such as banking and management systems. These applications are secure, scalable, and handle a large amount of data.
• Mobile Applications: Java is commonly used for developing Android mobile apps. It helps create apps that are reliable and work smoothly on smartphones.
• Embedded Systems: Java is used in devices like smart TVs and home appliances. It allows these devices to perform specific tasks efficiently.
• Smart Cards: Java is used in secure systems like ATM cards and SIM cards. It helps protect sensitive data and ensures safe transactions.
• Robotics: Java is used to program robots and automated machines. It helps control movements and perform tasks accurately.
• Games: Java is used to develop simple as well as complex games. It provides tools to create interactive and engaging gaming experiences.

sections.heading: Types of Java Applications
paragraphs: There are the following 4-types of applications that can be created using Java programming:

sections.heading: 1) Standalone Application
paragraphs: Standalone applications are also known as desktop applications or window-based applications. These are traditional software that we need to install on every machine. Examples of standalone applications are Media players, antivirus, etc. AWT and Swing are used in Java for creating standalone applications.

sections.heading: 2) Web Application
paragraphs: An application that runs on the server side and creates a dynamic page is called a web application. Currently, Servlet, JSP, Struts, Spring, Hibernate, JSF, etc. technologies are used for creating web applications in Java.

sections.heading: 3) Enterprise Application
paragraphs: An application that is distributed in nature, such as banking applications, etc. is called an enterprise application. It has advantages like high-level security, load balancing, and clustering. In Java, EJB is used for creating enterprise applications.

sections.heading: 4) Mobile Application
paragraphs: An application that is created for mobile devices is called a mobile application. Currently, Android and Java ME are used for creating mobile applications.

sections.heading: Java Platforms / Editions
paragraphs: There are four platforms or editions of Java:

sections.heading: 1) Java SE (Java Standard Edition)
paragraphs: It is a Java programming platform. It includes Java programming APIs such as java.lang, java.io, java.net, java.util, java.sql, java.math etc. It includes core topics like OOPs, String, Regex, Exception, Inner classes, Multithreading, I/O Stream, Networking, AWT, Swing, Reflection, Collection, etc.

sections.heading: 2) Java EE (Java Enterprise Edition)
paragraphs: It is an enterprise platform that is mainly used to develop web and enterprise applications. It is built on top of the Java SE platform. It includes topics like Servlet, JSP, Web Services, EJB, JPA, etc.

sections.heading: 3) Java ME (Java Micro Edition)
paragraphs: It is a micro platform that is dedicated to mobile applications.

sections.heading: 4) JavaFX
paragraphs: It is used to develop rich Internet applications. It uses a lightweight user interface API.

sections.heading: Prerequisite to Learn Java
paragraphs: To learn Java, you don't need to be an expert, but having a few basic things will help you a lot. First, you should understand how to use a computer, like creating files and folders. Basic knowledge of programming concepts such as variables, loops, and conditions is helpful, but not mandatory.

Knowing a little about any programming language (like C or Python) can make learning Java easier. You should also be familiar with installing software, because you will need to set up tools like the Java Development Kit (JDK).
Most importantly, you should have a logical thinking mindset and a willingness to practice, because programming is all about solving problems step by step.

sections.heading: Audience to Learn Java
paragraphs: The audience for learning Java includes students, beginners, and professionals who want to build a career in programming. It is suitable for anyone interested in developing applications like websites, mobile apps, or software, even if they have no prior coding experience.
